certified_calculation.actual_solution_normalization: u_lambda(4)=A_lambda(4)^(-1/4) for the actual DLMF recessive solution, after positive rescaling
certified_calculation.next_mathematical_gap: Replace the coarse compact Gronwall rectangle with a Bessel/Liouville--Green-preconditioned validated interval Taylor or equivalent sharp transfer enclosure before attempting Gamma_1 zero exclusion or continuation.

kappa_bracket.root_scope: at least one lambda=0 sign-changing zero; uniqueness is not assumed and nonzero-lambda kappa is allowed throughout the full fixed box

scientific_readout.computed_fact: For every fixed real (kappa,lambda) in root bracket 1 times either punctured lambda box, the explicitly normalized actual plus-recessive solution has a finite outward Q=-4 state rectangle and a complete-half-line finite Gamma_1 interval.
scientific_readout.interpretation: This removes the prior actual-solution/existence-and-boundedness null only at a deliberately coarse local-box level.
scientific_readout.open_hypotheses: Every nonzero-lambda Gamma_1 interval contains zero; no sign, zero, root continuation, uniqueness, spectral density, RAQ, C/H equivalence or physics conclusion follows.

certified_calculation.transport_method: LG actual-direction interval on Q>=4; rho invariant region to x=3; node-safe two-state infinity-norm Gronwall to Q=-4; rotating-frame Volterra/Gronwall to minus infinity

declared_conventions.compact_transport: Below x=3 use Z=(u,u_Q/kappa_min) and an outward matrix infinity-norm Gronwall envelope; this is analytic interval transport, not a numerical validated-ODE solver.
declared_conventions.execution: exact SymPy identities plus python-flint 0.9.0 Arb/acb outward balls; no floating-point ODE solve, root solve, quadrature, finite difference or sampling grid
declared_conventions.minus_tail: For Q<=-4 use the free-rotation frame (u,u_Q/kappa), variation of constants and integrable potential/forcing norms to enclose the infinite tail directly.
declared_conventions.plus_normalization: For each fixed real (kappa,lambda), rescale the actual DLMF recessive solution so u_lambda(4)=A_lambda(4)^(-1/4)>0; this fixes amplitude and leaves its logarithmic derivative unchanged.
declared_conventions.riccati_frame: r=-u_Q/u and rho=r-x-1/2, used only on x>=3 where the barrier proves rho in [-1,1] and u>0

exact_checks.statement: With C=6*pi^2 and x=C*exp(Q), the raw-C coefficient has the declared x form.
r=-u_Q/u and rho=r-x-1/2 obey the declared Riccati equation in Q.
At rho=1 the backward vector field is the negative of the upper barrier bracket.
At rho=-1 the backward vector field equals the lower inward margin.
The x-frame primitive gives the exact logarithmic amplitude bounds for constant rho barriers.
For Z_2=u_Q/mu, the second backward equation is Z_2,s=-(A/mu)Z_1.
The complete Q<-4 potential mass is 18*pi^4*exp(-8).
The complete Q<-4 forcing mass is 4*pi^2*exp(-6).
The free (u,u_Q/kappa) generator is skew and preserves the Euclidean norm.
The selected fixed-reference Wronskian obeys W_Q=-lambda*a*u*c_p.
The declared Gamma_1 is endpoint derivative minus the complete weighted minus-tail integral.
The inherited exact root bracket 1 is positive and lies strictly inside (2,3).

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: For each fixed real parameter in the declared boxes this selects an actual recessive solution, not the WKB proxy. The emitted Q=4 state interval encloses its normalized direction only on the declared box.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: The pinned upstream result proves A>0 and a finite uniform error-control budget on Q>=4. Its E<1 makes the actual recessive value at Q=4 nonzero, so a positive rescaling sets u(4)=A(4)^(-1/4) without changing the logarithmic derivative.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: Backward evolution has u_s=r*u>0 while u>0; hence u cannot reach a node before x=3 and the Riccati continuation is noncircular. No no-node statement is made below x=3.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: The executable checks put rho(4) in [-1,1], prove both boundary vector fields point inward for 3<=x<=C*exp(4), and give r=x+1/2+rho>=x-1/2>0.
theorem_guards.theorem: Scalar inward-barrier continuation for a locally Lipschitz Riccati equation

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The resulting endpoint rectangle encloses the actual state through any nodes. It is a coarse analytic interval transport, not a validated numerical ODE trajectory or a sharp endpoint evaluation.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: On the compact interval Q0<=Q<=Q3 the exact state system has induced infinity norm at most mu+A_abs/mu, with positive finite mu=kappa_left and an executable finite coefficient envelope.
theorem_guards.theorem: Variation of constants and the scalar Gronwall inequality for a bounded linear two-state system

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: The complete infinite minus-tail remainder and declared Gamma_1 are bounded for the constructed normalized actual solution. The broad interval contains zero and gives no continuation, eigenvalue, spectral or RAQ conclusion.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: In (u,u_Q/kappa) the free generator is skew. V and a have the executable finite masses 18*pi^4*exp(-8) and 4*pi^2*exp(-6), respectively, for Q<=-4.
theorem_guards.theorem: Free-rotation variation of constants plus Gronwall on the half-line

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: Containment checks only regress the coarse analytic envelope. They do not claim that the envelope reproduces the narrow Bessel endpoint or prove uniqueness of the bracketed root.
theorem_guards.hypotheses: At lambda=0 the exact recessive solution is K_(i*kappa)(C exp Q); Arb evaluates the full inherited kappa band and applies the identical u(4)=A_0(4)^(-1/4) normalization.
theorem_guards.theorem: DLMF modified-Bessel equation and derivative recurrences

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: A finite numerical enclosure is not a raw-C spectrum, C/H quantum equivalence, quantum-gravity result, observation or TOE claim.
